newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-SOUTHALL SET TO STEP DOWN AFTER 91 WALES CAPS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-SOUTHALL SET TO STEP DOWN AFTER 91 WALES CAPS.

text.p: Wales' record-breaking goalkeeper Neville Southall acknowledged that his international career is probably over after Belgium killed off his chances of appearing in next year's World Cup finals in France.
After losing 2-1 to the visitors, Southall, 38, said he may now bow out after winning 91 caps.
"It is highly probable this is my last game," the Everton goalkeeper said.
"I am not going to go to a World Cup and, shame though that is, you cannot turn back time. I think it would be pretty pointless to continue.

"People have said I should go on and get 100 caps but I feel that if I did that I would be cheating my country and the lads who are waiting behind me for their chance. Perhaps now is the best time for them to gain valuable experience."

Although Wales still have a mathematical chance of reaching the finals, their appearance there is highly unlikely. The Netherlands lead group seven with 12 points, followed by Belgium on nine and Wales on seven. Both the Dutch and the Belgians have played two matches less than Wales.
Belgium coach George Leekens was delighted with the victory set up by a 25-metre shot from Bertrand Crasson after 24 minutes and a diving header from Lorenzo Staelens a minute before half-time.
Although Wales scored through a Gary Speed header half-way through the second half, Belgium hung on for all three points.
Leekens added: "We have had a tough few months, but there is a lot of new hope.
"Tonight I saw an emphasis on team play which is vital for Belgium. This win hasn't changed everything but there are things which went wrong before which we put right tonight."
Strikers Luis Oliviera-Barroso and 18-year-old Lokonda M'Penza also caused the Welsh problems with Brazilian-born Oliviera-Barroso coming close to adding to the lead.
Wales became more desperate as their hopes faded and they brought on John Hartson for Dean Saunders after 65 minutes.
Two minutes later they pulled a goal back when Speed headed home but that was never going to be enough.
